summary: Nira Wickramasinghe is a historian and Indologist who studied at Paris-Sorbonne University, the University of Paris, and the University of Oxford (D.Phil 1989). She taught at the University of Colombo (1990–2009) and became Chair of Modern South Asian Studies at Leiden University in 2010.

Nirajan Kafle is an Indologist who completed his doctorate at Leiden University in 2015 under Peter C. Bisschop, having also studied under Diwakar Acharya, Bhim Kandel, and Kashinath Nyaupane. He held posts at the Nepal Research Centre, Leiden, and Ashoka University.

Niran Rajvamshi works in the fields of Indology and history and archaeology. In 2018, Rajvamshi was affiliated with the National Archives of Nepal and served as an editorial board member for Documenta Nepalica.

Niranjan Prasad Chakravarti (1893–1956) was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Calcutta and the University of Cambridge under Edward James Rapson. He served extensively in the Archaeological Survey of India, including as Director General of Archaeology (1948–1950).

Niranjan Saha is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies who completed a doctoral thesis at the University of London in 2014, having studied under S. Padmanabhan, Gayethri Peetha, and Umamaheswari. Saha was affiliated with Kaliachak College in 2020.

Nirbhay N. Singh is a scholar of religious studies and psychiatry. He has served as Director of the Commonwealth Institute for Family Studies, Professor at Virginia Commonwealth University, and Clinical Professor of Psychiatry and Health Behavior at Augusta University (attested 2015–2018).
Nirmal C. Sinha was an editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology, with posts attested in 1978 and 1988.

Nirmal Chandra Sinha (1911–1997) was a historian and Tibetologist educated at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta. He served as the founder director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (1958–1987) and Centenary Professor of International Relations at Calcutta (1971).
Nirupam Chakma is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College (attested 2015) under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing.
Nitin Kumar Jain is an Indologist who earned his PhD at Central Sanskrit University, where he was appointed Assistant Professor in 2019.

Nityanand Misra is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the Indian Institute of Management, Bengaluru (~2005–2007) and under the traditional teacher Rāmbhadrācārya (attested 2016).
Nivitigala Sumitta Thero works in Buddhist and religious studies, completing a PhD at the University of the West (2014–2023). In 2022, he became the founder and CEO of Dhamma USA.
Noa Gal is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who earned a Doctor of Philosophy degree at the University of Oxford under the supervision of Richard Gombrich (attested 2003).

Noa Ronkin is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology who completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (2003) under Richard Gombrich, also studying with Shlomo Biderman. She served as a Lecturer and Research Fellow at Stanford University.
Noah Avigan is a scholar in Indology and religious studies, affiliated with Yale University's Religious Studies department as a graduate student (attested 2026).

Noboru Karashima (1933–2015) was a historian and Indologist educated at the University of Tokyo (B.A., M.A., D.Litt.). He held academic posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, the University of Tokyo (1964–1994), and Taisho University (~1994–2008).

Noboru Miyata (1936–2000) was a scholar of folklore, religious studies, and history who studied at Tokyo University of Education and the University of Tsukuba. He held professorial posts at Tokyo Gakugei University, the University of Tsukuba, and Kanagawa University.
Noboru Ueda is a scholar of Buddhist studies who held posts at the University of Tokyo (attested 1990) and Mejiro University as a professor (attested 2015).

Nobuchiyo Kotani is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Otani University and Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama and Hajime Sakurabe, later serving as professor at Otani University (~1988–2013) and president of its junior college.

Nobuhiko Kobayashi is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University under Yutaka Ochihara. Kobayashi held posts as assistant professor at the University of Toronto (1969) and Kyoto University (1979), and lecturer at Taisho University.
